podcast.title: 21st Century Tweetpop Descendant
podcast.body: Girl in Red is identified as a 21st-century artist whose Bedroom Pop sound is a direct descendant of the various forms of Tweetpop. This modern genre is enabled by affordable and powerful laptops, along with accessible recording software and microphones, allowing for the creation of dreamy, introspective, sensitive, and vulnerable music. "We wouldn't have artists like Girl in Red or Beba Dooby or Arlo Parks, Rex Orange County, and Sockermummy if it wasn't for the various flavors of Tweet Pop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bedroom Origins in Norway
podcast.body: Marie Ulvin Ringheim, known as Girl in Red, began her musical journey in her bedroom in Horton, Norway, after her father gifted her a USB microphone for her laptop, marking a quintessential start for a bedroom pop artist. "She started making music in her bedroom in Horton, Norway after her father gave her a USB mic for her laptop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: SoundCloud Debut as Lydia X
podcast.body: Before finding wider recognition as Girl in Red, Marie Ulvin Ringheim initially posted her songs on SoundCloud using the pseudonym Lydia X, highlighting the platform's role in the early development of bedroom pop artists. "Soon, she started posting songs on SoundCloud using the name Lydia X."

xref.body: Rex Orange County is identified as a 21st-century artist in the Bedroom Pop genre, a style that owes its existence and characteristics (dreamy, introspective, sensitive, vulnerable) to various forms of Tweetpop. This musical approach is enabled by the affordability and power of modern recording equipment, such as laptops and software. "We wouldn't have artists like Girl in Red or Beba Dooby or Arlo Parks, Rex Orange County, and Sockermummy if it wasn't for the various flavors of Tweet Pop."

xref.title: 21st Century Tweetpop Descendant
xref.body: Sockermummy is listed as a 21st-century artist whose "Bedroom Pop" output is a direct descendant of Tweetpop. This genre thrives thanks to cheap and powerful laptops, recording software, and microphones, allowing for intimate, personal, dreamy, introspective, sensitive, and vulnerable music that echoes the Tweetpop sensibility. "We wouldn't have artists like Girl in Red or Beba Dooby or Arlo Parks, Rex Orange County, and Sockermummy if it wasn't for the various flavors of Tweet Pop."
